newsitem.title: USA: Amgen third quarter earnings rise sharply.
newsitem.headline: Amgen third quarter earnings rise sharply.

text.p: Amgen Inc. Tuesday reported a 23 percent increase in third-quarter earnings, which were boosted by higher sales in its two drugs.
Profits for the third quarter ended Sept. 30 rose to $179.5 million, or 64 cents a share, from $145.8 million, or 52 cents a share.
Earnings in the latest quarter include a 3 cents-per-share tax credit, resulting from a change in accounting practices at its Puerto Rican manufacturing plant.
Total revenues rose 15 percent to $567 million.

The sharp sales increase included a 19 percent rise in sales of Epogen, a red blood cell stimulating drug, and a 12 percent jump in sales of Neupogen, used to increase white blood cell count in cancer chemotherapy patients.
Epogen sales totaled $274 million in the quarter and Neupogen sales reached $259 million.

Profits beat analysts' consensus prediction of 59 cents per share. Amgen stock, which had settled down $3.69 at $59.875 during the daily trading session on Nasdaq, rose about $1.625 in after-hours trading after the earnings were released.

"This was another solid quarter, and strong earnings continue to drive further development of Neupogen and Epogen as well as advance clinical development of Amgen's 12 potential products being studied in human trials," Chairman Gordon Binder said in a statement.
Binder said the company's spending on research and development during the quarter rose 24 percent to $130 million.

While sales of the company's existing drugs were strong, Amgen also reported some disappointments in the drug development area. It said trials of platelet-stimulating factor MGDF to treat acute myeloid leukemia were not promising.
Amgen, which has said it foresees an eventual slowdown in Neupogen and Epogen sales, is aggressively seeking to offset that with new drugs.
